chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from a man, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When you raise your head from the bowing (ruku'), straighten your back, for there is no prayer for the one who does not straighten his back.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on straightening the back after ruku' in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi emphasizes the physical integrity of the prayer posture, linking the validity of salat to the proper alignment of the spine after ruku'. In Shia jurisprudence, this is often interpreted as a requirement for 'iqamah al-sulb' (straightening the back) to ensure the transition between postures is complete and dignified, reflecting the spiritual composure required in worship.
